title: Lahaina Disaster Recovery Update Meeting: January 17, 2024

recap.headline: Lahaina debris removal begins as agencies update sewer, water, air and permits
recap.in_60_seconds: County, state and federal agencies gave their weekly Lahaina recovery update on January 17, 2024, while the Mayor was in Washington, D.C. No residents spoke during the program; questions were taken one-on-one after the meeting. The Army Corps of Engineers said debris removal on Lahaina residential lots began that morning, with a goal of clearing the first 100 properties within 30 days, and that all 25 Kula properties are now done. EPA will start inspecting about 99,000 feet of Lahaina sewer lines in early February, and the County said sewer service could return down to Puamana in about a month. The County expects to pick a firm to help with expedited rebuild permits around February 16 and open a Lahaina permit office by the end of March. A plan on landlords evicting tenants to lease units to FEMA, and the location of a permanent ash and debris site, are still to come.

parts.title: Opening and Lahaina Advisory Committee update
parts.presenter: County of Maui communications staff; Lahaina Advisory Committee member
presented: The Mayor was in Washington, D.C. meeting with the federal delegation to seek support.
The advisory committee said it is passing community input on housing and natural and cultural resources to its subcommittees and agencies.
Three Lahaina Advisory Committee members were honored on the opening day of the state legislature.

parts.title: Maui Emergency Management Agency update
presented: The agency is running lean, with four staff positions helping operations and a six-person EMAC team supporting the emergency operations center.
Phone system problems are believed to be fixed; the main number is 808-270-7285.

parts.title: FEMA update
presented: FEMA is securing 200 more apartment units for its direct lease program.
FEMA has heard of people being evicted from homes not hit by the fire so owners can lease to FEMA or other programs; the Mayor and Governor are looking into it.
Background checks are required by unit owners, but FEMA plans to house people even if they fail one; over 1,000 people are eligible for FEMA programs.
Recovery work will pause for the January 20 Unity Walk.

More information on a plan to address evictions

parts.title: Army Corps of Engineers debris removal update
parts.presenter: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers commander
presented: Debris removal on Lahaina residential lots began this morning; seven crews should be working by January 24, aiming to clear the first 100 properties within 30 days.
Priority goes first to lots next to homes that did not burn, then to lots with higher environmental risk such as near the shoreline; owners get at least 72 hours' notice and can watch.
Dust is controlled with water, air monitors and sealed, lined trucks; no air monitor alarms went off today or on the 25 Kula properties, which are now 100% complete.
The Olowalu temporary debris storage site began receiving material today; work on the temporary school near Kapalua Airport continues despite rain.

next.what: Two more crews start on additional properties

parts.title: EPA sewer line inspection mission
parts.presenter: EPA incident commander for water mission
presented: EPA's hazardous waste removal (Phase 1) is complete and that team has left.
EPA will inspect about 99,000 linear feet of Lahaina sewer lines, which were plugged to keep salt water from killing the treatment plant's microorganisms.
Inspections take about 30 days, then data goes to the County to prioritize repairs; occupied homes get at least 48 hours' notice.

parts.title: Department of Environmental Management wastewater update
presented: Pump stations 5, 6 and 7 are running again but are being tested for automatic operation.
The treatment plant is still fragile; biological treatment will be added, and sewer service could return down to Puamana in about a month.

In Wahikuli, owners who build a septic system will have to connect to the new County sewer line within 180 days of notice under Maui County Code 14.21A.010; the department is willing to work with the Council on changing that.

next.when: in the next month or so

parts.title: Department of Water Supply update
presented: The water advisory for Area 4D will be amended this Friday after delays from fire debris.
Maps will add a green crosshatch for large multi-unit properties with fire-damaged buildings; residents there should check with their property manager or association.
Areas 5 and 6 cover about 1,800 service laterals and several miles of pipe.
Removed meters will be replaced free when owners rebuild.

parts.title: American Red Cross shelter update
presented: About 5,400 people in about 2,400 households are in 32 sheltering sites.
Most residents of the 110 habitable homes have moved back; air purifiers, cleanup kits and masks are available.
Some people in shelters and condos are being moved to hotels to free up units for long-term leasing.

parts.title: Department of Health environmental update
parts.presenter: Department of Health Deputy Director for Environmental Health
presented: DOH contracted near-shore beach sampling and is entering an agreement with the University of Hawaiʻi to test fish.
Soil samples in Lahaina showed elevated arsenic, lead and cobalt, lower than in Kula; the ash is toxic.
There are 40 purple air sensors and e-BAMs, including 28 sensors and 10 e-BAMs in Lahaina, plus four asbestos and heavy-metal samplers.
Air data is posted at fire.airnow.gov.

next.what: Clean Air Branch installs about 12 more sensors in Lahaina and 8 in Olowalu
Results of air sampling during Lahaina debris removal

parts.title: Office of Recovery expedited permitting update and closing
parts.presenter: County Managing Director, Office of Recovery
presented: The County will hold community meetings on the permanent ash and debris containment site.
Expedited permitting will cover the first home and first accessory unit with an allowed accessory structure on each lot, and needs code changes through the Council.
A firm to help review permits should be chosen around February 16, with a Lahaina permit office open by the end of March.
The County intends to let construction start before water and sewer reach a lot, aiming for service by move-in.

moments.who: County of Maui Managing Director leading the Office of Recovery
moments.quote: about the public sentiment analysis that was done in coordination with our FEMA partners, about all the testimony and feedback that we've been hearing from the community, Ideas, policy suggestions, and things of that nature, as well as helping you folks understand what the engagement process will look like in that long-term recovery plan and how you can stay engaged throughout it to help make decisions for the future of Lahaina.
moments.about: In January 2024 the county said it would soon share a FEMA-assisted analysis of community feedback and explain how residents can take part in shaping the Lahaina long-term recovery plan.
